# `set_control_value`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Set one camera control (gain, exposure, target temperature and others) by name.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / probable (64-bit build; 32-bit build probable) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xe89a0, SetControlVal @0x11dff0, camera SetControlVal @0x153ac0, special ids and map find @0x153c9c..0x153c34, per-id setter @0x151c50 (64-bit build); camera library control-set dispatch and exposure-to-lines conversion, from its debug information; ISP exposure branch calls ASI_ISP_SetManExpGain, HPC branch calls ASI_CAM_SetHPC, CoolerOn "on" branch additionally calls the fan-speed setter with camera-library control id 22 (64-bit build); confirmed unchanged in firmware 9.75 (identical instruction counts, relocation-only differences, both 64-bit and 32-bit builds) |

Sets the named camera control under the camera lock. On the 64-bit build, the exact spelling TargetTemp additionally updates a cached target temperature and persists a camera-specific setting; other casings resolve the control but skip that special case (32-bit build casing behaviour not established). Exposure and gain changes queue delayed configuration writes before the lower-level setter reports success, so a failed call does not establish that nothing changed. The ISP exposure control divides the effective integer by one million before the SDK call; the inspected ISP gain branch logs and reports success without an SDK gain update. Values are integers in fixed units (READ, camera library, except exposure), namely exposure in microseconds (INFERRED); gain in tenths of a dB on multiplicative-gain sensors, raw analogue gain otherwise; offset in raw black-level units; target temperature in degrees C, clamped to -40..30; cooler power in percent; red/blue white balance as a gain with 100 as unity, affecting only pixel format 3. The name is matched without regard to case against the imager's control-name table (26 real entries, ids 0..25; a static scan of the table also reads one further row past id 25, which is a scan artifact, not a 27th control id). Gain, Exposure, Red, Blue and MonoBin are handled specially (MonoBin only stores the mono-bin setting); any other name must resolve to an id in the device's control table (see get_controls), otherwise 210. The device makes no range check against the get_controls limits; out-of-range handling is the camera library's and is unresolved. Setting Temperature (read-only) returns success with no effect (READ, 64-bit build). Gain, Exposure, Red and Blue (device ids 0, 1, 19, 20) map to camera-library control ids 0, 1, 3 and 4; CoolPowerPerc, TargetTemp and CoolerOn (device ids 5, 6, 7) map to camera-library control ids 15, 16 and 17. Setting CoolerOn to an "on" value additionally sets camera-library control id 22 (fan speed) to 255 or 127, depending on a condition not further resolved. ISP_Exposure (id 25) scales by 1/1,000,000 before the same library call as Exposure; ISP_Gain (id 24) only logs and makes no library call (as above); HPC (id 23) calls the library's hot-pixel- correction control. Confirmed unchanged in firmware 9.75 on both the 64-bit and 32-bit builds (identical instruction counts; only relocation differences).

Side effects: Changes camera controls; queues or persists per-page control settings (and the target-temperature setting) possibly before a later failure; no rollback is established.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"set_control_value"`. [READ] |
| `params` | object\|array | yes | - | Control name and value, as an object {name, val} or as a positional array [name, val] (further array elements ignored). Absent, null or scalar params give an empty map and hence 105. `name` is required and matched case-insensitively against the camera's exposed controls. `val` is an integer, boolean (stored as 0 or 1), float (stored at single precision; rounded to the nearest integer for the camera call) or string. A missing `val` is not rejected by the handler (it takes an internal sentinel); a null, object or array `val` gives 109. Units are fixed per control (exposure microseconds, INFERRED; gain tenths of a dB on multiplicative-gain sensors; offset raw black level; target temperature degrees C clamped to -40..30; cooler power percent; red/blue gain with 100 as unity; READ, camera library). Several listed controls are accepted with no effect (see set_control_value). Per-control range checking beyond the target-temperature clamp is unresolved; read the limits from get_controls. [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (both) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |

| `code` | integer | yes | - | (success) Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (success) Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 105 | name missing or not a string (including absent, null or scalar params) | `expected string param` |
| 109 | val is null, an object or an array | `unexpected param` |
| 318 | Camera absent or closed, or unavailable camera id | `device not connected` |
| 210 | Name unknown, or its id not in the device's control table (for example Bandwidth, Gamma) | `not supported` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

Failures inside the camera setter are not an exhaustively audited closed list; the handler forwards whatever application code the helper set. Camera library return codes are internal and never reach the wire; a library failure is reported as a fixed application code, typically 318. Limits come from get_controls but are not enforced by the device; library handling of out-of-range values is unresolved.

## Example

Request, gain - Object form (values invented):

```json
{"id":50,"method":"set_control_value","params":{"name":"Gain","val":80}}
```

Request, positional - Positional form:

```json
{"id":51,"method":"set_control_value","params":["Exposure",10000]}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"set_control_value","result":0,"code":0,"id":50}
```

Reply, bad-val:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"set_control_value","error":"unexpected param","code":109,"id":52}
```
